{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a left-facing fish with a body outline and forked tail. Before the push, about 111 of 115 standing dominoes were connected to the start, with only a few stubs left by the crossing. I haven't seen the result of the push, so I can't say the judge recognized it. My direct contribution was the upper tail fin, stroke 4, which was laid and dark. I did not add the eye Sofia asked for, so the picture is a little less distinctive than it could have been. I also didn't pick up the pad or take on a second job once my fin was done, which was a missed chance to add more.

Execution: I finished my fin and kept my hands off the crossing once Sofia and Omar were working there. I was less effective on the nose joint. I said twice that I'd nudge it, then couldn't find the gap. Hana diagnosed the problem (the first curve domino was too steep) and put in the bridge, so the fix was hers, not mine. I also spent time on status messages that repeated what others had already said, and that time could have gone to the eye.

Collaboration: I kept the lines of ownership clear. I took the upper fin, stayed clear of others' areas and avoided double-work. I also credited Sofia, Hana and Omar for their specific catches (the nose bridge, the stray spike, the crossing gap). Where I overreached, I said so and backed off.

Leadership: Sofia set the plan and led the table, and Hana did the most careful checking. I mainly supported them by keeping morale up and giving the manager clear summaries. I called for hands-off before the push to avoid bumps. I could have led more by volunteering for the eye, or by checking the nose joint more closely before announcing I'd fix it."}
